models_evaluated: eight open-source small language models (names not given in the text)

links.outcome: Comparison of fine-tuned open-source SLMs against commercial LLM baselines on ED triage, referral, and diagnosis tasks
links.effect: LoRA fine-tuned open-source SLMs outperformed Claude Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 baselines on triage level and specialist referral; diagnosis prediction remained challenging for open-source SLMs.
links.quote: Using 2,083 MIMIC-IV-ED cases and Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 as baselines, we found that LoRA fine-tuned open-source SLMs outperform commercial baselines on triage level prediction and specialist referral recommendation, while diagnosis prediction remains challenging for open-source SLMs.

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking fine-tuning strategies (zero-shot, prefix tuning, LoRA, full fine-tuning) for small language models
Deploying locally hosted open-source small language models instead of closed-source commercial LLMs to reduce privacy risk

screen.reason: The paper benchmarks fine-tuning strategies for locally deployable small language models on emergency department clinical tasks using the MIMIC-IV-ED dataset, comparing technical model accuracy against commercial baselines rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
